description: SimGrid is a framework for building simulators of distributed applications running on distributed platforms, used to prototype, evaluate and compare platform configurations, system designs and algorithms. It provides ready-to-use, experimentally validated models and APIs for commodity clusters, wide-area and local-area networks, peer-to-peer systems, data centres, grids, clouds and HPC with MPI applications, and its models are fast with a low memory footprint so that large simulations run on one machine. It is developed by an international research team led from French institutions such as Inria and CNRS, has supported hundreds of publications over twenty years, and the current release is 4.1. Coverage: user-described platforms of any size, from a single cluster to wide-area networks, with no built-in geographic data. Format and access: C++ library with C, Python and Java interfaces for Linux, macOS and Windows, with documentation and source on the website and GitLab; free of charge under the LGPL. Caveats: it simulates resource sharing and flows, not packets, so protocol-level detail is lower than in packet simulators; platform descriptions must be written by the user. Simulation uses: capacity planning and optimisation of data-centre and distributed computing platforms, network flow at flow level, and resilience studies of distributed services under failures. Related records: CloudSim and CloudSim Plus are cloud-specific alternatives, while ns-3 covers packet-level detail.
